main_strengths: High school fidelity: the 'does the event add or remove intervention, credit or price distortion?' test is applied in nearly every item, and the mechanisms fit the event (liquidation vs forbearance, moral hazard in the weekend bank merger, money substitutes in the stablecoin run, interest rates as coordinating signals under YCC, state-directed malinvestment in the China stimulus), one or two per item rather than a checklist.

Analogs are real, dated before 2025, and mostly apt and accurately described (Buenos Aires truce 2018, Trump-Juncker 2018, Miller Fed 1978, Credit-Anstalt 1931, Knickerbocker 1907, Reserve Primary 2008, Fed 1942 peg, RBA YCC 2020, EU solar duties 2013); only one clear misfit (US 1974-75 rents).

Good news is no longer forced into the crisis story: the trade truce is read as removal of intervention (equities LONG, USD SHORT, gold NEUTRAL), productivity as genuine growth, and boom-phase events (dovish BoE, YCC, BoJ purchases) get equities/credit LONG with a later-correction caveat. Equities LONG in 5/19, bonds balanced 7 LONG / 7 SHORT / 5 NEUTRAL.

Non-US events usually name their channel to US/global assets (sterling to dollar, yen carry, EM dollar funding, China commodity demand); event-vs-backdrop contradictions are stated; tool calls are clean JSON; no backdrop numbers appear before get_macro_data.
Gold NEUTRAL is reasoned in the 4 items where it should be (liquidation-phase cash demand, strong dollar plus deflation, high real funding costs).
main_problems: Gold LONG is still largely a teacher default: 15/19 LONG (11 at conviction 4), never SHORT, and the only top-conviction signal in 7/19. It is argued from the event in about 7 items (negative real rates, dovish BoE, bank rescue, interbank stress, stablecoin failure, YCC, BoJ purchases) but asserted without a monetary channel in about 7 (lithium closure, 5% lithium tariff, productivity jump, rents, G7 housing bust, job openings, frontier hyperinflation via US assets). The template stance 'favours hard assets' is the likely cause.

Credit SHORT in 14/19: justified by a bust-type top scenario in about half; elsewhere it contradicts a growth-up S1 (payroll beat), the trajectory's own 'credit may rally briefly' (China stimulus), or the event's small scale (lithium tariff).

Conviction does not scale with event size or reach: the 5% lithium tariff gets the same equities/credit SHORT 3 + gold LONG vector as a mine closure removing a large share of world supply; an RBA hike, one EM's IMF request, a 150bn China package and a frontier hyperinflation get conviction 3-4 on US/global assets, often against the trajectory's own 'country-specific' sizing. High convictions are often carried by the US backdrop (recession, wide HY), not the event.

Templated scenarios: 3 scenarios in 17/19, top probability exactly 0.45 in 14/19 (0.55 in 4), and a recurring 'liquidation / policy rescue (growth up, inflation up) / contagion' triad (rescue scenario in 9/19).

Asset universe and horizon undefined: signals mix local and US/global assets (frontier local bonds/equities/credit next to DXY and gold; gilts or Treasuries for the BoE item), scenario axes mix local and US growth, and short-run boom support is mixed with long-run bust calls (bailout put ignored; YCC bonds SHORT 'vulnerable to correction' while the peg holds in S1).

Instruction echoes the student will learn: 'the event gives no bp, pp or share-of-GDP magnitude' in 15/19 first [Think]s, 'newest (marginal) information' in 14/19, 'does not contradict the backdrop' in 10/19, 'a single backdrop cannot show a trend', spurious contradictions (BoJ cap vs US curve), 'Causal chain: event ->', and two one-line second [Think]s.

Non-Austrian inflation logic in 5-6 items (wage-push, cost-push; rents or a single input treated as general inflation), and the backdrop's most Austrian feature, the real policy rate (e.g. 1.0% vs 7.8-8.0% CPI, or 5.5% vs 0% CPI), is rarely named. Average HY spreads (451-511bp) are called 'elevated'.
Second [Observe] JSON broken or mangled in 3/19 (always the 'US 2y-10y spread (bp)' key), not caught by validate(); with loss on all assistant tokens the student learns to write these blocks.
suggested_prompt_or_template_changes: templates.toml [school.austrian].signals: replace 'favours hard assets' with a conditional: gold LONG only when the event adds money/credit creation, debases a currency or undermines trust in bank/fiat liabilities, or the backdrop shows deeply negative real rates; in a liquidation the demand for money (cash, bills, dollars) rises and gold can be NEUTRAL; a shock to another commodity is not a gold signal. Require the gold reason to name that channel.

Add a scope step to rule 1 (US/global-systemic, regional, sector-specific, local to a non-US economy) and cap conviction at 2 on US/global assets for sector or local events unless a large channel is named; tag each template's scope in templates.toml and have validate() flag conviction >= 3 on sector/local templates.

Rule 5: define the six signals as US/global benchmarks (US equities, Treasuries, DXY, gold in USD, WTI, US credit) over a fixed horizon matching the evaluation (e.g. 3 months); local assets and later-phase effects go in the chain; scenario growth/inflation directions refer to the US/global economy unless labelled 'local'.

Probabilities: ask for a top probability set by the evidence (about 0.6-0.7 for mechanical, well-understood events, 0.35-0.4 when genuinely ambiguous); extend signal_report() with a histogram of top probabilities and scenario counts, warning when one value exceeds about 40% of a batch.

Reword rules 1 and 4 so the teacher stops narrating compliance: 'use the event's size if it gives one, otherwise judge scale from what it touches; do not comment on missing units' and 'mention a contradiction with the backdrop only if there is one'. Add the echo phrases ('gives no bp', 'does not contradict', 'newest information', 'single backdrop', 'I do not infer a trend', 'Causal chain: event ->') to META or a soft filter.

Austrian diagnosis line: add 'read the real policy rate (policy rate minus CPI) and money growth first: is credit artificially cheap or already tight?' and 'a relative-price change (rents, one input, wages) is not inflation; a general price rise needs money and credit growth'. This anchors gold/bond calls in the backdrop and removes wage-push/cost-push logic.

validate(): flag credit SHORT when the top scenario is growth-up, and gold LONG >= 3 when the top scenario is disinflationary with USD LONG, unless the reason names a horizon or monetary channel; consider rejecting items where gold is the only top-conviction signal and the chain never mentions money, credit or debasement.

Write the second [Observe] deterministically from the backdrop (it is a pure echo), or json.loads it and check keys/values; give v3's second-[Think] rule a content check (>= 25 words, not just 'I need the backdrop').

Training: train.py puts loss on the whole assistant reply, so the student learns to write the episode list itself. Mask [Observe] spans or check analogs against a vetted episode list (the US 1974-75 rent analog in syn-a0001 does not fit).
